report.source_text: Twenty-four hours later, he underwent surgery. An open repair via supra-infraumbilical incision was performed. Intraperitoneal access to the aorta was obtained via dislocation of the colon and small intestine. The lesion was included into a giant omentum sac, and was extremely fragile and hemorrhagic due to the chronic inflammatory process, and a covered rupture was revealed (Figure 4). We found 4 liters of ascites and blood in the peritoneal cavity.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 43-year-old man with sickle cell anemia and remote splenectomy presented with fever and ascites. Initial CT revealed massive ascites and a giant paraaortic mass. CTA confirmed a 9.8 cm splenic artery stump aneurysm with arteriovenous shunt causing early venous filling and splenic vein enlargement (indicating portal hypertension). Diagnostic paracentesis was performed. He underwent emergent open surgical repair 24 hours after admission, revealing a covered rupture with 4 liters of hemoperitoneum. Six days postoperatively, he developed fever, elevated inflammatory markers, paralytic ileus, and anemia. CT/DSA at 10 days postoperative demonstrated hemorrhagic pancreatitis with minor gastric bleeding. He was treated for sepsis in the ICU for 20 days and discharged in good condition following abdominal closure.
